title: OpenAI-compat: unify rate-limit semantics, idempotency keys, and error codes
author: Maya Chen
description: Summary: This PR standardizes rate-limit semantics and error responses in the OpenAI compatibility layer, introduces a consistent idempotency-key contract for requests (including streaming/long-poll flows), and unifies error codes returned to clients so downstream SDKs and customers observe stable behavior. Motivation: We discovered inconsistent 429 + Retry-After behavior across endpoints and ambiguous idempotency semantics for streaming reconnects which caused duplicate operations and poor client retry behavior. This caused support escalations (SUP-1123) and flaky canary results when toggling routing fallbacks. Changes: 1) Add middleware that emits a consistent Retry-After header and machine-readable JSON body field ("retry_after_seconds") for 429 responses; 2) Define a canonical error schema for the OpenAI-compat path: {"code": "string", "message": "string", "type": "client|server|rate_limit|auth|invalid_request"} (represented here in docs and errors.go); 3) Implement idempotency-key handling middleware that: a) accepts Idempotency-Key header on POSTs and PATCH-like ops, b) persists operation metadata for the configured TTL (default 24h) keyed by idempotency key, c) returns 409 with standardized body when a conflicting request is detected, and d) exposes an Idempotency-Status header ("reused|completed|in-progress") to help SDKs decide next steps; 4) Extend streaming endpoint logic to attach idempotency metadata to streamed sessions and gracefully handle client reconnects by allowing resume semantics where the resumed token references the same idempotency key — this avoids duplicate model invocations for reconnects within the key TTL; 5) Map OpenAI legacy error strings to the new canonical codes and include backward-compatible message hints; 6) Update SDK compatibility layer (python) to surface the Retry-After numeric value and Idempotency-Status and to document correct retry/backoff behavior. Testing & rollout: unit tests cover middleware and error mapping; integration tests simulate concurrent clients hammering rate limits; new e2e streaming test validates resume + idempotency across simulated reconnects. CI had an initial flaky e2e streaming run (rerun passed). Rollout uses feature-flag gating on the openai-compat route with a gradual canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) and a manual fallback to legacy path if anomalies appear. Backwards compatibility: clients that ignore new headers get the same high-level HTTP statuses but may miss idempotency hints; we keep a compat mapping for six months and emit deprecation warnings in responses. Migration notes: SDKs should adopt Idempotency-Key on mutating calls and honor Retry-After; see docs/openai-compat/error-handling.md for code samples.

release_notes: Standardize OpenAI-compat error and rate-limit semantics: clients should expect a numeric Retry-After header and a stable error schema. Idempotency-Key support added for mutating and streaming flows to prevent duplicate operations on reconnects. Backwards compatible but clients should update SDKs to use new headers for best behavior.
